chapters.title: Secrets: keeping passwords out of the code

takeaways: GitHub Actions runs automation defined in a plain YAML workflow file stored in the repository's .github/workflows folder, started by events such as a push, a pull request or a schedule.
Jobs run in parallel on fresh runner machines while the steps inside a job run in order, and ready-made marketplace actions and reusable workflows keep most files short.
Passwords and tokens belong in repository, organization or environment secrets with minimal permissions, and public repositories run on standard runners for free.
hook: Testing and shipping code by hand is where mistakes slip through, yet many beginners assume automation needs servers and a DevOps team. This Simply Explained episode walks newcomers through GitHub Actions step by step: workflow files, events, jobs, runners, marketplace actions, secrets and costs, so you can read a workflow and explain what it does.
